headline: Prioritize access: eliminate login failures and investigate the rising access complaint signal.
memo_markdown:
## Recommendation
Make **access** the next-quarter priority. Fix `access.login_failure` first, focusing on sign-in failures and false “no internet” errors; use the broader access complaint signal to identify additional access blockers.

## Evidence
Access complaints have high reported severity: mean severity is 3.853333 [A038], and 81.33% are severity 4+ [A042]. Access’s share of complaints rose from 1.21% in the early trend window [T003] to 1.75% in the late window [T006]. The specific `access.login_failure` issue has 115 complaints [C025] and mean severity 3.886957 [C027]. Reviews describe being “unable to log in” (91b3f409-7fcf-472b-a308-29361707085e) and a sign-in error reporting no internet (c4da3f91-0e39-4eb9-b992-43c75ed5ca66).

## Alternatives considered
Playback has a larger complaint burden, 653 [A015], and higher mean severity, 3.192956 [A017], but its complaint share declined from 7.18% [T033] to 5.13% [T036]. Its `playback.playback_stops_or_skips` issue is significant at 301 complaints [C013], but the trend does not make it the clearest next-quarter priority. Billing/support has 932 complaints [A008], but the top `billing.premium_paywall` issue reflects perceived restrictions on basic listening [C001]; billing/support’s complaint share rose from 4.04% [T009] to 13.97% [T012], so it remains a strong alternative. Usability has the largest area complaint count, 1,280 [A001], but lower mean severity, 2.528906 [A003], and a lower severity-4+ share than access, 1.48% [A007].

## Limitations
Evidence covers completed review records: 9,996 [K002], with 4 quarantined [K003]; the analysis uses complaint and cancellation records only [K005]. Public reviews are self-selected and are not representative of the customer population. Cancellation mentions express intent, not observed churn. Trend windows exclude the partial first and last months; complaint shares use completed records as their denominator. Broad or unresolved classifications may conceal specific access problems.
